content: SQLite :memory: (official + mattn FAQ + issue threads): every :memory: connection gets its own private empty database; database/sql pools multiple connections so a second pooled connection sees no tables or missing writes (intermittent no such table). Fixes: pin SetMaxOpenConns(1), or URI file::memory:?cache=shared for same-process sharing; named private shared DBs: file:memdb1?mode=memory&cache=shared (share only with identical name; removed when last connection closes). Shared-cache memory DBs cannot be shared across processes. Taking an explicit sql.Conn from a max-1 pool blocks further pool calls until released. Official pragma docs: journal_mode for an in-memory database is only MEMORY or OFF and cannot be changed; attempts to set WAL are ignored, not an error. So :memory: must not assert WAL actually engaged. WAL is impossible for in-memory DBs.
